question: How many letters in the arrangement are immediately preceded by a symbol and immediately followed by a symbol? Arrangement (left to right): E A # / @ Q # M D N C $ O G ^ # # Y F Q W.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 8; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: Scan each letter and its two neighbors. Only Q has symbols on both sides (@ and #).

question: How many symbols are immediately preceded by a letter and immediately followed by another symbol? Arrangement (left to right): G U * M B + £ L Q C ( % @ H O D K > X Z F # & Y.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 9; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The parenthesis in C ( %, plus in B + £, and # in F # & are the three qualifying symbols.

question: How many letters are immediately preceded by a symbol and immediately followed by a number? Arrangement (left to right): T 8 & W 8 # Q 6 R & P T & 6 Q 9 $ D 8 @ 7 H % Y 3 G 5 $ 9 %.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 10; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: W, Q, D, and Y are respectively in &W8, #Q6, $D8, and %Y3. No other letter meets both neighbor conditions.

question: How many letters are immediately preceded by a number and immediately followed by a symbol? Arrangement (left to right): # 3 P # 9 I N M P 2 @ R $ K 7 % 8 T 2 ( 5 Y $ ) # 6 J 4 3 M K 7 T E @.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 11; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: P in 3P# and Y in 5Y$ are the only letters with a number directly before and a symbol directly after.

question: How many numbers in the arrangement are not immediately followed by a symbol? Arrangement (left to right): 6 K 5 % L T 8 B 4 G 9 # E Q 7 G 5 $ 9 % U P 3 T 8 & W H 6 R.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 13; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: Numbers followed by non-symbols or the end are 6, 8, 4, 7, 3, and 6. The remaining five numbers are each followed by a symbol.

question: If the unit's digit of each number is interchanged with its hundred's digit, which original number becomes the largest? Numbers from left to right: 721, 463, 227, 316, 627.
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 4; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The transformed numbers are 127, 364, 722, 613, 726. The maximum is 726, from original 627.

question: How many letters lie between the second letter of the first word from the left and the first letter of the first word from the right? Arrangement: CAR HAT FED EYE.
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 5; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: Ignoring spaces, the selected letters are A at position 2 and E at position 10. Positions 3 through 9 contain seven intervening letters.

question: If all vowels are removed from the arrangement, which element is twelfth from the left? Arrangement: A E C B % 7 D $ E B 5 C ? 3 D E 9 @ 2 #.
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 6; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: After removing A and both E's, the first twelve remaining elements are C, B, %, 7, D, $, B, 5, C, ?, 3, D. The twelfth is D.

question: In the arrangement, which element is sixth to the left of the fourteenth element from the left? Arrangement: Q R 4 $ 3 K H I M D 5 © N E J 8 I # T V U % W 6 & B A 7 2 F P.
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 7; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The fourteenth element is E. Six places left is position 8; position 8 contains I.

question: If the first and last digits of each number are interchanged, which original number becomes the smallest? Numbers: 348, 436, 652, 198, 563.
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 8; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: Swapping endpoints produces 843, 634, 256, 891, and 365. The smallest transformed value, 256, comes from 652.

question: Which letter is twenty-first from the left in the English alphabet?
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 9; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: A is position 1; counting to position 21 gives U.

question: Which letter is ninth to the left of the fifteenth letter from the left in the English alphabet?
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 11; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The 15th letter is O. Nine positions left is position 6, F.

question: Which letter is fourth to the right of the seventh letter from the left in the English alphabet?
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 12; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The 7th letter is G; advancing four places gives K.

question: Which letter is eighth to the right of the twelfth letter from the left in the English alphabet?
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 13; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The 12th letter is L. Eight places after L is position 20, T.

question: Which letter is fourth to the right of the fourteenth letter from the right end of the English alphabet?
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 14; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The 14th letter from the right is M (position 13 from the left); four places right is Q.

question: In the arrangement R B 7 5 E % M 2 W 4 8 Q 9 # B 2 A S M S, which element is third to the right of the twelfth element from the left?
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 12; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The twelfth element is Q. Moving right three positions gives 9, #, B.

question: Which element is seventh to the left of the third element from the right? Arrangement (left to right): @ J @ 1 # 2 K 3 6 $ L 2 4 2 R 6 4 2 G 5 2 $ 0 4 2 %.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 14; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The third from the right is position 24 (4). Seven positions to the left is position 17, which also contains 4.

question: How many 5s are immediately preceded by an even number and immediately followed by an odd number? Sequence: 3765783245548791534863598764.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 15; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The 5 in 6-5-7 qualifies. The first 5 in 4-5-5 also qualifies. The other 5s fail one of the parity conditions.

question: How many 3s are immediately preceded by 7 and immediately followed by 9? Sequence: 72963739773973221339373939.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 16; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The sequence contains the block 739 three times, and each block contributes one qualifying 3.

question: What is the sum of the eighth number from the left and the fifth number from the right? Arrangement (left to right): 65 67 87 86 & 43 32 37 @ 27 % 29 76 71 49 $ 52 23 #.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 17; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: Counting numbers only gives 27 as the eighth from the left and 76 as the fifth from the right. Their sum is 103.

question: How many numbers in the arrangement are perfect squares? Arrangement (left to right): 4 7 1 9 0 5 3 8 2 6 1 4 7 9 2 0 3 6 8 5 1 2 7 3 4.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 19; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The one-digit perfect squares present are 0, 1, 4, and 9. They occur 2, 3, 3, and 2 times respectively, totaling 10.

question: What is the difference between the squares of the fourth number from the left and the third number from the right? Arrangement (left to right): 5 8 3 1 7 0 4 6 2 9 5 3 8 1 7 4 0 2 6 9 3 5 1 8 7 4 0 2 6 9 3 5 1 8 7.
source: Alphanumerical test 01_.pdf, PDF page 18; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The fourth number from the left is 1 and the third from the right is 1; 1²−1²=0.

question: Which letter is fourteenth from the right end of the English alphabet?
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 10; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: Fourteenth from the right is 26−14+1=13th from the left, M.

question: Consider the sequence A2, D6, H12, M20, S30. Which pair comes next if the letter gaps continue increasing by one and the number pattern continues?
source: Original SSC-style practice question
independent_reasoning: Letter jumps are +3,+4,+5,+6, then +7: S→Z. Numeric terms are n(n+1) for n=1 through 5, so next is 6×7=42.

question: The paired terms follow two rules: B2, E4, I8, N16, T32. What is the next pair? Letters advance by successively increasing steps and numbers double; the alphabet cycles after Z.
source: Original SSC-style practice question
independent_reasoning: Letter increments are +3,+4,+5,+6, so next is +7 from T; wrapping after Z gives A. The number doubles from 32 to 64.

question: Reverse the word BIRD and then replace each letter by its English-alphabet position. What code results?
source: Original SSC-style practice question
independent_reasoning: BIRD reversed is DRIB. D=4, R=18, I=9, B=2.

question: Apply this rule to each letter-digit pair: advance the letter by one alphabet position and decrease the digit by one. What does A3, C5, E7, G9 become?
source: Original SSC-style practice question
independent_reasoning: Applying the explicit transformations yields A3→B2, C5→D4, E7→F6, and G9→H8.

question: In A 4 # B 9 @ C 16 $ D 25 %, how many perfect-square numbers are immediately preceded by a letter and immediately followed by a symbol?
source: Original SSC-style practice question
independent_reasoning: 4, 9, 16, and 25 are all perfect squares; each sits between a letter and a symbol. All four qualify.

question: Starting from the fifteenth letter from the right in the English alphabet, move 4 places right, then 6 left, then 7 right, then 3 left. Which letter do you reach?
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 16; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: R15 is L; four right gives P; six left gives J; seven right gives Q; three left gives N. The choices G,K,F do not include N.

question: Which letter is three places to the left of the letter four places to the right of the sixteenth letter from the left in the English alphabet?
source: Alphanumerical test 02_.pdf, PDF page 15; exam/year not stated
independent_reasoning: The 16th letter is P. Four positions right gives T, then three positions left gives Q.
